# dsh-aux-degrade
**Compaction summaries and session titles stop burning their output budget on reasoning.**
> ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up upd
**DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates.
> 🟢 **Collision risk: very low.** It occupies **one server-side seam (`llm/stream`) and no client sl
ot** — only **4** plugins here share that seam, and it touches **auxiliary calls only** (compaction
summaries, session titles), never the main conversation request. See Compatibility.
**English** · 简体中文
## What this is
Besides the main conversation, a DSH session has a pile of **auxiliary LLM calls** running behind th
e scenes: generating compaction summaries, starting session titles, enhancing prompts.
They share the same model as the main conversation, yet often **specify no reasoning effort** — so t
hey inherit the high level you set and burn the entire output budget on reasoning. The result is tha
t a compaction summary is cut off halfway by `max_tokens`, and that truncation is **silent**: nothin
g reports an error, the next turn simply starts with a piece of context missing. A session title tha
t tops out halfway and turns into half a word is the same disease.
`dsh-aux-degrade` hooks into the `llm/stream` waterfall and scales the auxiliary call down before it
degrade` hooks into the `llm/stream` waterfall and scales the auxiliary call down before it is sent.
## The four things it does
All four happen inside the same `llm/stream` hook. **Note: only #1 is controlled by the `enabled` sw
itch**; #2–#4 execute under any configuration — this is deliberate, because they fix problems like "
an upstream plugin omitted required information", not optional optimizations.
### 1. Lower the reasoning effort to `off`
If any one of the following conditions holds, this call's `reasoningEffort` is overridden to `off`:
| Criterion | Description |
| **By purpose** | `purpose` falls in the `purposes` list (by default covering `compaction`, `sessio

n-title`, `title`) |
| **By originating plugin** | the initiator is in the `auxPlugins` list (by def

ault recognizing `dsh-prompt-enhance`) |
| **By shape** | `purpose` is not declared and `tools` is n
ot an array — a call of this shape is auxiliary |
**And** the caller itself has not explicitly specified `reasoningEffort`. If it set a level itself,
this plugin lets it through and does not override someone else's explicit intent.
To use a different level instead of `off`: `config.effort = 'low'` and the like.
### 2. Raise `maxTokens` to no less than 1024
Some callers set `maxTokens` extremely small (worst case 1) together with a high reasoning level, wh
ich amounts to "truncated before the body even starts".
This plugin gives it a floor: **no less than 1024**. It can be overridden with an environment variab

### 3. Append two faithful-preservation requirements to the compaction instruction
The biggest risk of a compaction summary is not "short", it is "lossy". Under pressure a summary gen
erator prioritizes narrative and drops hard facts: paths, commands, error codes, constraints.
Whenever this call has `purpose === 'compaction'`, the plugin appends two sections to the end of the
compaction instruction:

**Idempotent**: if the instruction already contains these two sections, they are not appended again.
### 4. Clear `tools` on compaction calls
A compaction summary does not need to call any tool. Keeping the tool definitions both consumes prom
pt space and gives the model the opportunity to "just call a tool while it is at it" — which turns w
hat should be a plain-text summary generation into multiple round trips.
For calls with `purpose === 'compaction'`, `tools` is cleared. It can be turned off with `config.noT
`purpose === 'compaction'`, `tools` is cleared. It can be turned off with `config.noTools = false`.

## 9. The official-patch notice: one dialog, naming the patch and how to apply it
The one official patch this plugin **requires** (`pi-ai-max-tokens-floor`, editing `dist/api/simple-
options.js` inside `@earendil-works/pi-ai`) is announced by **this plugin itself**, in one dialog.
Why it is required: upstream pi-ai clamps `max_tokens` to 1, so auxiliary calls (compaction summarie
s, session titles) can come back with one or two characters — and whatever the summary never covered
really does disappear from the context. This plugin can turn the high thinking level off and raise
the floor from the plugin layer, but **it cannot change that clamp** (the third-party dist exposes a
read-only ESM namespace).
- **How to apply it (any one of three)**: **A** press "Copy the prompt" and hand it to **your own ag
ent**; **B** `node apply.mjs --check`, then `node apply.mjs --apply --only pi-ai-max-tokens-floor`;

**C** apply by hand with `git apply -p1`;
- **The patch library**: <https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh

-patch-library>;
- **Detection**: a **content hash** (`pristine` / `patched`) plus the `*.orig` back

up; when it cannot decide it says **"cannot tell"** and never guesses "applied";
[该节后续省略]
### Why is `dsh-prompt-enhance` recognized by default?
Because when it initiates a call it **does not pass `purpose`** — the "by purpose" criterion above i
s completely ineffective for it. Without this `auxPlugins` criterion, its calls would inherit the hi
gh reasoning level all the way through, the output budget would be eaten by inference, and the sympt
om would be a flood of 502s and half responses. This criterion exists for its sake.
## Compatibility
### 🔗 With `dsh-capability-composer`
No direct coupling.
